newsitem.title: USA: Triton settles with SEC in bribe violation.
newsitem.headline: Triton settles with SEC in bribe violation.

text.p: Triton Energy Corp. has agreed to pay $300,000 in penalties to settle charges that it violated federal securities laws in connection with its alleged role in foreign bribery payments, regulators said Thursday.
Triton did not admit or deny the allegations, the Securities and Exchange Commission said.

The SEC filed a civil complaint in U.S. District Court in Washington against Triton and Philip Keever and Richard McAdoo, both former senior officers of the company's Triton Indonesia subsidary, for violating the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.

The complaint alleges that in 1989 and 1990, McAdoo and Keever authorised numerous improper payments to Roland Siouffi, Triton Indonesia's business agent acting as an intermediary with the Indonesian government agencies.

The SEC alleged the payments were for the purpose of influencing specific actions by various Indonesian government agencies. To conceal the true purpose of the payments, employees created false documents indicating the funds were used for legitimate purposes.
The SEC charged McAdoo and Keever along with other employees concealed these payments by falsely documenting and recording the transactions as routine business expenditures.

Keever, 62, of Dallas, agreed to the settlement without admitting or denying the allegations and fined $50,000 in civil penalties. Keever is a former commercial manager, vice-president and general manager and president. He retired in January 1996.

McAdoo, 42, of West Linn, Ore., has not offered to settle with the SEC. McAdoo was vice president and general manager until his termination in December 1989. The SEC is seeking an injunction and civil penalties.

Four other former Triton officials, agreed to cease and desist from future federal security violations without admitting or denying allegations for their alleged role regarding improper payments or false records.

David Gore, 55, was a director and former president of Triton Energy Corp; Robert Puetz, 55, was a vice-president of finance and chief financial officer of Triton Energy. William McClure, 44, was a contract auditor with Triton Indonesia and Robert Murphy, Jr., 58, was a certified public accountant and controller of Triton Indonesia.
Triton, based in Dallas, is engaged principally in the exploration and production of crude oil and natural gas. Triton Indonesia is a wholly-owned subsidiary whose assets were sold on May 31, 1996.
Triton's stock edged down 37.5 cents to $42.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
